title: Review of Computation of Monthly CPF Interest Payment
what_it_is: Review of Computation of Monthly CPF Interest Payment

sections.label: CPF SMRA interest rates
sections.summary: CPF members receive 4.08% per annum on SMRA savings in first quarter 2024, plus extra interest on combined balances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the SMRA-pegged rate currently exceeding the 4% floor rate, Central Provident Fund (CPF) members will receive 4.08% per annum interest on their SMRA savings in the first quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government continues to pay 1% of extra interest on the first $60,000 of combined CPF balances for all members, as well as an additional 1% extra interest on the first $30,000 of combined CPF balances for members aged 55 and above.

sections.label: CPF interest rate review
sections.summary: The Government will continue to review CPF interest rates periodically to ensure their relevance in the prevailing operating environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to review CPF interest rates periodically to ensure their relevance in the prevailing operating environment.

sections.label: CPF floor rates sustainability
sections.summary: The Government has paid 2.5% Ordinary Account minimum and 4% SMRA floor rate over two decades, a more sustainable computation method.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, the Government has paid 2.5% minimum interest on the Ordinary Account savings and 4% floor rate for the SMRA savings over the past two decades, in spite of the protracted low interest rate environment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you do a like-for-like comparison, without the 4% floor rate, the SMRA interest rate would have been an average of 3.2% per annum or about 0.8% points lower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The reassurance that I want to give to the hon Member and also Members of the House is that this is a more sustainable method of computation over the longer haul, compared to investing in shorter-term, more volatile instruments.
